title: Cutline milestones & scope-freeze playbook for API/Console/Runtime release integration
creator: Ava Chen
description: Purpose: Define a deterministic set of milestones, cut criteria, and communication playbooks to coordinate the next API + Console + Runtime release window. Goal is to reduce last-minute scope churn, align cut decisions across Eng/Design/PM, and publish release notes with consistent content for customers and sales.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A published milestone calendar (feature freeze, code freeze, release candidate, GA) shared with Eng/Design/Support. 2) A concrete, prioritized list of cut criteria with examples (performance regressions, security blockers, compliance gaps). 3) A templated release-notes draft that maps features to owners and risk level. 4) Runbook for emergency rollback and opt-down model variants.
tasks: Draft milestone calendar and communication cadence
Hold cross-functional kickoff with eng leads + design + support
Collect feature owners and map risk to cut criteria
Define gating checklist (perf SLOs, regressions, security sign-off)
Create release notes template and column mapping for Console / API / Runtime
Schedule weekly cut reviews starting 3 weeks before GA
comments: 2025-03-21: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to three-phase milestone: Soft Freeze (features but no schema changes), RC Freeze (no API contract changes), GA. Action: Diego to circulate calendar and invite eng leads.

2025-03-25: Engineering update (ENG-4812): preliminary perf regression metric for batching change currently +8% median latency under certain payloads. Decision: treat as 'investigation required'—if not remediated by RC Freeze, mark as cut candidate.
2025-03-28: Design feedback: Console release notes require a short 'impact' blurb and screenshot for any UI changes. DES-214 assigned to prepare screenshots for the top 3 console UX changes.

2025-03-31: PM review: compiled ticket list for potential scope cuts. Prioritized by customer exposure and rollback complexity. Link to draft spreadsheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xExampleSharedLink

2025-04-01: Security note: engineering requested a security review for the new KMS integration path. Security team flagged encryption-at-rest upgrade; security_review_required set to true for that subitem. Action: schedule security review by 2025-04-06. (See GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/security/issues/112)

2025-04-02: Decision log: Adopted 'two-strike' cut rule—if a feature fails two gating checks (perf or security or compatibility) after RC Freeze, it is removed from GA and moved to the next minor release. Noted trade-off: longer stabilization vs. feature breadth.

2025-04-02: Next steps: finalize release notes template, get sign-off from support on customer-facing language, and publish internal timeline by 2025-04-05. Assigned owners updated in the shared sheet.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Late-breaking perf regressions in KV cache changes could push above latency SLOs. Mitigation: require performance regression sign-off from runtime benchmark owner and maintain a togglable conservative kernel path for GA.
Risk: API contract changes introduced by last-minute schema edits. Mitigation: block schema-modifying PRs after Soft Freeze unless approved by API guild and mark as hotfix-only.

Risk: Inconsistent release notes across Console and API causing customer confusion. Mitigation: single source of truth spreadsheet with assigned owner per item and a weekly sync to reconcile language.
Risk: Dependencies on Dedicated infra autoscaling improvements (ENG-4999). Mitigation: include fallback capacity plan and clear rollback criteria if autoscaling experiments are unstable.
communication_plan: Weekly update email to stakeholders (PM/Eng/Design/Support/Sales) every Friday starting 2025-04-04.
Status channel in Slack: #rel-1-20-updates for day-to-day decisions and urgent blockers.
Public-facing release notes draft for Customer Success and Sales by 2025-04-10 for review.
Internal dry-run demo of Console & API changelog for Support on 2025-04-14.
decision_history: 2025-03-21: Chosen milestone structure (Soft Freeze -> RC Freeze -> GA) to balance integration time and QA.
2025-04-02: Two-strike cut rule adopted for deterministic cut decisions.
2025-04-02: Agreed that any feature with a security flag must have explicit security sign-off before RC Freeze.
